You can ask the question in actual language and get an answer, and it basically is a knowledge graph of your organization. So you can ask any question. Think of ChatGPT for your enterprise. Ask any question about your enterprise. (01:03:45): So people understand search because they understand Google and you put in a query and then you refine it. But chat interfaces, people still don't really know how to use. If you look at the stats from ChatGPT, from what I understand, the retention is fairly low. People use it, they play with it, and then they don't get back to it because it's not in their workflow and they have a hard time figuring out what they can and can't do for it. When I got to Glean the first week I met with the assistant quality team and one of the biggest issues they have is people trying to use Glean for things that there's no way it could know. Like what should my top priority be next week when we don't even know what your priorities are. But then there's golden cases that are just amazing. (01:04:44): The example of refining queries and searched years for people to understand how to do. And it took a lot of features of auto complete and refinements at the bottom of the page. So we need to build in those things, guardrails to help with the change. To help suggest, oh, Lenny, here's what you could do. Here's a prompt to find out the status of your feature that Tamar built. So how do you give people guardrails so that they understand what is going to work and what isn't going to work? Because this whole, I don't know what I can ask. And then on top of that, the non-deterministic. An enterprise CIO will go use ChatGPT on the weekends, but they come to work and they expect their software to be deterministic. So how do you help educate users about that? (01:05:34): And then the other thing I'll say about using LLMs is the industry is transforming so rapidly that you need to make sure that your product gets better as the LLMs get better. And that too many people are building things to make up and compensate for the LLMs that all that work is going to go away. So it's okay to do it to understand that it's going to go away, but that can't be your differentiator. You have to understand that your differentiator is something that will continue to be there as the LLMs get better and smarter.
turns.zh: 刚加入Glean的第一周，让我深刻认识到很多东西。但首先，我得先向那些可能不了解Glean的人解释一下它的业务。Glean最初是作为企业搜索工具开发的。它能读取你使用的所有SaaS应用的内容，比如微软、谷歌、Slack、Salesforce、Jira等工具，将这些内容索引化并支持搜索。起初它只是一个基于AI的企业搜索引擎，采用BERT模型和向量嵌入技术。毕竟Glean的早期工程师来自谷歌，而谷歌开发BERT就是为了提升搜索质量。因此，使用ML技术进行搜索是顺理成章的。之后，GPT3引入了自然语言界面和聊天界面，你可以用自然语言提问并获得答案，实质上就是企业的知识图谱。用户可以针对企业提出任何问题。这就像是为企业打造的ChatGPT。（01:03:45） 人们理解搜索是因为熟悉谷歌的搜索逻辑——输入查询并进行筛选。但聊天界面至今仍未被广泛使用。根据我的了解，ChatGPT的用户留存率相当低。人们尝试后发现它不符合工作流程，就不再使用了。刚加入Glean的第一周，我与助理质量团队交流，他们面临的最大挑战之一是，用户试图让Glean完成超出其能力的任务。比如，用户问“下周我的首要任务是什么”，而我们根本不知道他们的优先事项是什么。不过也有成功案例，比如优化查询和搜索年份功能，这些都需要借助自动补全和页面底部推荐功能。我们需要构建这些保护机制，帮助用户理解哪些功能可行，哪些不可行。比如，“莱尼，建议你可以这么做。”或者“塔玛尔开发的功能状态查询提示语。”那么如何为用户设置这些保护机制，让他们清楚哪些方法可行，哪些不可行呢？因为用户总在说“我不知道能问什么。”此外，非确定性因素也很头疼。企业CIO可能周末用ChatGPT，但上班后却期待软件能提供确定性结果。如何帮助用户理解这一点？（01:05:34） 另外，使用LLM的另一个挑战是，行业发展太快，产品需要随LLM技术进步而迭代。太多人为了弥补LLM的不足而临时拼凑，然而这些努力最终会白费。因此，理解LLM技术会过时固然重要，但这不应成为你的核心竞争力。你必须明白，随着LLM技术的进步和智能化，你的差异化因素必须持续存在且优于他人。

turns.speaker: Lenny
turns.en: And as part of that, because the LLMs get so much smarter, everyone else will become awesome. And to keep up, you need something that is actually outside of the LLM that continues to differentiate you and is better than what other people are doing.
turns.zh: 因此，随着LLM技术的日益强大，竞争对手也会变得越来越强大。要想保持领先，你需要开发出超越LLM技术的差异化功能。

turns.speaker: Tamar Yehoshua
turns.en: Well, yeah. That your whole product gets better as the LLMs get better.
turns.zh: 没错，随着LLM技术的进步，整个产品也会不断优化。

turns.speaker: Lenny
turns.en: That makes sense.
turns.zh: 这说得在理。

turns.speaker: Tamar Yehoshua
turns.en: It's a frame of a of mind of how you approach the value add you're having.
turns.zh: 这是一种思考方式，告诉你如何看待自己所创造的价值。

turns.speaker: Lenny
turns.en: Awesome. Tamar, to close out our conversation, is there anything else that we did not cover that you think is important to share or you think might be helpful to leave listeners with before we get to our very exciting lightning round?
turns.zh: 太棒了。塔玛尔，在我们结束对话之前，还有什么我们没有讨论过但你认为很重要、值得与听众分享的内容呢？在我们进入激动人心的闪电问答环节之前。

turns.speaker: Tamar Yehoshua
turns.en: I in my decades of working in tech, have never been working in an environment that's moving so quickly and it's really exciting. It's super energizing and it's also scary. But you have to change how you're working. You have to change how you're working so that you can keep up because it's going to be an interesting decade ahead with all these new tools that are coming out. And staying ahead will be hard, but it's also, there's so much I think richness and opportunity here. So I advise people to get in the thick of it and try it out because you'll be surprised at how many products we can build.
turns.zh: 在我几十年的科技工作生涯中，从未在一个变化如此迅速的环境中工作过，这真的令人兴奋。它充满活力，但也令人感到压力。你必须改变工作方式，以便跟上节奏，因为未来十年将出现许多新工具，保持领先将是一项挑战。不过这里也蕴藏着巨大的机遇和财富。所以我建议大家积极投身其中，亲自尝试，因为你会惊讶于我们能开发出多少产品。

turns.speaker: Lenny
turns.en: I love that. I can't help but drill in one level deeper. Is there anything you found to help you stay ahead and help you stay aware of what's happening? Are there newsletters you find useful? Chat, podcasts that just help you keep up to date on where things are going? Is it like a person you look to like, "Hey, what's new?"
turns.zh: 我很赞同。我忍不住再深入一层。有什么方法能帮助你保持领先、了解行业动态吗？有没有你觉得有用的时事通讯？聊天群、播客之类的，能让你及时掌握行业动态？有没有你特别关注的人，比如“嘿，最新动态是什么？”

turns.speaker: Tamar Yehoshua
turns.en: There are definitely AI newsletters that I look at. There's AI podcasts that I listen to. I now have a commute, so in some ways that's good because I get to keep up on the AI podcasts. So I just try and listen. I'm trying to build some prompts for myself to make it easier to say ... Take in ... I haven't perfected this, but the ChatGPT voice mode where you can load it. Somebody who I just hired it at Glean was saying he does this. He loads up stuff before his commute and then he'll be like summarize these articles and then he can ask questions to it. So I need to up my game there. But I definitely have a list of Ben's Bites and The Neuron. Those are good summaries and I like Gil and Sarah Guo's podcast. I listen to Cognitive Revolution. There's too many of them right now, but I pick and choose.
turns.zh: 我确实会关注一些AI相关的时事通讯和播客。我现在通勤路上有时间听，所以这挺好的。我会努力建立一些提示机制，让自己更容易获取信息……我还没完全掌握，但ChatGPT的语音模式很不错，你可以上传内容。Glean刚招来的某位员工说他用这个功能。通勤前上传一些文章，然后让它总结内容，再提问。这方面我还需要提升。但我确实订阅了Ben's Bites和The Neuron。这两个总结得不错，我还喜欢Gil和Sarah Guo的播客。我听Cognitive Revolution。现在这类播客太多了，但我会挑选收听。

turns.speaker: Lenny
turns.en: Awesome. Okay. We'll link to those ones you just mentioned in the show notes. We'll have Gil and Sarah Guo's podcast, it's called No Priors. I was actually just listening to it on the way here. Sarah is going to also be at Lenny's and Friends Summit. She's going to be moderating a panel between Kevin Weil and Mikey Krieger who are the CPOs of Anthropic and Open AI. So there we go. Another quick plug for lennyandfriendssummit.com. I think it's lennyssummit.com.
turns.zh: 太棒了。好的，我们会在节目笔记中附上你刚刚提到的这些链接。Gil和Sarah Guo的播客叫No Priors。我刚来这儿的路上还在听。Sarah也会参加Lenny's and Friends Summit。她将主持Kevin Weil和Mikey Krieger的讨论，他们分别是Anthropic和Open AI的首席产品官。好的，再快速宣传一下lennyandfriendssummit.com。我想应该是lennyssummit.com。

turns.speaker: Tamar Yehoshua
turns.en: Awesome.
turns.zh: 太棒了。

turns.en: With that Tamar we've reached our very exciting lightning round. Are you ready?
turns.zh: 好了，塔玛尔，我们进入激动人心的闪电问答环节了。你准备好了吗？

turns.speaker: Tamar Yehoshua
turns.en: I am ready.
turns.zh: 我准备好了。

turns.speaker: Lenny
turns.en: Okay, let's do this. First question, what are two or three books that you have recommended most to other people?
turns.zh: 好的，开始吧。第一个问题：你向别人推荐得最多的两三本书是什么？

turns.speaker: Tamar Yehoshua
turns.en: So one book was recommended to me by Shashir, the CEO of Cota. When I started at Slack, he recommended the book Switch: How to Change Things When Change Is Hard by Chip and Dan Heath. And it's such a good book. And it's about how do you set a path for people to follow. It's the whole elephant and the rider. So setting the path but yet motivating people to go down the path. And I read it. We had an all hands about ... I don't even remember the topic. It was something that we were like all up in arms about that we had to do. And I had just read the book and after the all hands I went up to store it and I'm like, "You did that all wrong. You need to read this book. That is not how to get people motivated." And he read the book and he's like, "You're right." So it just changes how you think in organizations to affect change. So that's on the organizational leadership. And one book I really liked was a Team of Rivals. It's a book about Lincoln and putting together his cabinet during the Civil War. One, I just learned a lot about the Civil War that I didn't really know. And it's about, again, a book about leadership and it is fascinating.
turns.zh: 科塔（Cota）的首席执行官沙希尔（Shashir）曾向我推荐过一本书。当我刚加入Slack时，他推荐了奇普·海斯（Chip Heath）和丹·海斯（Dan Heath）的《开关：当改变变得困难时如何行动》。这本书太棒了。它讲的是如何为人们设定前进的路径。这就像是"大象与骑手"的故事——既要设定路径，又要激励人们沿着这条路走下去。我读了这本书后，我们开了一次全体会议……我甚至不记得讨论的主题了。当时我们对某件事争执不下，必须要做决定。我刚读完这本书，会议结束后我去把书收起来时，我对他说：“你做得完全错了。你应该读这本书。这才是不让人们丧失积极性的正确做法。”他读了这本书后说：“你说得对。”这本书能改变你在组织中推动变革的思维方式。这就涉及到组织领导力了。还有一本我非常喜欢的书是《对手的团队》。这本书讲的是林肯在内战期间组建内阁的故事。我不仅对内战有了很多不曾了解的认识，而且这本书还探讨了领导力问题，读起来非常引人入胜。

turns.speaker: Lenny
turns.en: I don't think anyone's recommended either of these. So love them. Next question, do you have a favorite recent movie or TV show you really enjoyed?
turns.zh: 我觉得没人推荐过这两本书。所以我很喜欢它们。接下来问题：你最近有没有特别喜欢的电影或电视剧？

turns.en: I don't know if you like British murder mysteries.
turns.zh: 不知道你是否喜欢英国的谋杀悬疑剧。

turns.en: I don't know either.
turns.zh: 我也不确定。

turns.speaker: Tamar Yehoshua
turns.en: It's a niche thing, but there's a guy named Anthony Horowitz and the latest series he did was called Magpie Murders. And it's just an intricate story so I enjoyed it.
turns.zh: 这类题材小众，但有个叫安东尼·霍洛维茨（Anthony Horowitz）的人，他最新创作的系列叫《喜鹊谋杀案》。这是一个错综复杂的故事，所以我很喜欢。

turns.speaker: Lenny
turns.en: Very niche but amazing. Do you have a favorite product you've recently discovered that you really like?
turns.zh: 非常小众但很棒。你最近有没有发现什么特别喜欢的产品？

turns.speaker: Tamar Yehoshua
turns.en: Well, I'm going to give two. One is tech and one is non-tech. So non-tech I really like dark chocolate.
turns.zh: 嗯，我要推荐两个。一个是科技类的，一个是非科技类的。非科技类的，我特别喜欢黑巧克力。

turns.speaker: Lenny
turns.en: Actually just like a dark chocolate bar.
turns.zh: 其实就是黑巧克力棒。

turns.speaker: Tamar Yehoshua
turns.en: A really good dark chocolate that's simple. Like no frills, none of this. Just dark chocolate. And I discovered this chocolate called Bisou chocolate. It's a guy in Oakland who makes it himself. Super niche. He was selling at the farmer's market. And it's just like if you want like a simple play, no nuts, no anything just-
turns.zh: 一款非常好的黑巧克力，很简单。没有花哨的装饰，什么都没有。就是纯黑巧克力。我发现了一款叫Bisou的巧克力，是奥克兰的一个小伙子自己制作的。超级小众。他在农贸市场上卖。这款巧克力就像是，如果你想要一款简单的，没有坚果，没有任何添加剂的——

turns.speaker: Lenny
turns.en: No sea salt.
turns.zh: 没有海盐。

turns.speaker: Tamar Yehoshua
turns.en: Great pride in the beans he resources them from.
turns.zh: 他对采购的咖啡豆非常自豪。

turns.speaker: Lenny
turns.en: Wow. It's called Bisou with a B?
turns.zh: 哇。Bisou这个名字带个B？

turns.speaker: Tamar Yehoshua
turns.en: Yeah. Bisou as in Kiss in French. And then on the tech side, the honest answer is Glean. I was listening to your podcast with Nikita who said that people over 22 don't use new products except at work. And that stuck with me. The new products I usually use are at work and I use Glean 10, 15 times a day. I use it so much and it changed the way I onboarded. It changed the way I work. Even the simplest questions, you don't bother people, you don't interrupt people on Slack. You're like, "What's the latest status with this deal? What's the last time we talked to them?" I meet somebody at a conference and I can quickly say, "Have we ever talked to this company before?" And I can just get an answer. Or without asking an engineer, "Where's the latest design doc?" It has really transformed how I work. So I know it's cheating in that it's the product I work on, but it's the actual honest answer.
turns.zh: 是啊。“Bisou”在法语里是"吻"的意思。技术方面来说，老实说，我会选Glean。我听了你和尼基塔的播客，她说22岁以上的人除了工作场合外基本不使用新产品。这句话让我印象深刻。我日常使用的新产品基本都在工作中，而且我每天会用Glean 10到15次。它彻底改变了我的入职流程和工作方式。即使是最简单的问题，比如在Slack上不打扰别人，不随意打断别人，你也可以快速询问：“这笔交易的最新进展如何？上次和他们沟通是什么时候？”在会议上遇到新人时，我能迅速查明：“我们之前和这家公司合作过吗？”无需询问工程师，就能获取最新设计文档。它彻底改变了我的工作方式。虽然Glean是我所在的公司产品，但这确实是诚实的回答。

turns.speaker: Lenny
turns.en: And for folks that haven't heard of Glean, it's one of the most successful B2B AI companies out there. It's like a very large successful business and company that if you haven't checked it out, you should definitely check it out.
turns.zh: 对于不了解Glean的人来说，它是目前最成功的B2B人工智能公司之一。这是一家非常成功的大型企业，如果你还没了解过它，真该去试试看。

turns.speaker: Tamar Yehoshua
turns.en: As our investors say, it's one of the AI companies that's actually making money.
turns.zh: 正如我们的投资者所说，这是少数真正能盈利的人工智能公司之一。

turns.speaker: Lenny
turns.en: Very few of those. Awesome. Two more questions. Do you have a favorite life motto that you often come back to, repeat yourself, share with friends or family and work or in life?
turns.zh: 非常少见。太棒了。再问两个问题。你有没有最喜欢的的人生格言，经常回味、反复告诫自己、与朋友家人分享，或者用于工作和生活中的？

turns.speaker: Tamar Yehoshua
turns.en: I have one that my father told me when I was being really indecisive about what college to go to. He was really bored of the conversation and he said, "There are no right decisions. You make a decision right." And it is so true. Because you never know what's going to happen in life. You just have to commit to whatever you're doing and have no regrets about it. You can't be like, "Oh," 10 years later, "what if I had taken that job over there?" It's like you make your success based on how you approach the decisions that you've made.
turns.zh: 我父亲曾在我犹豫不决选择哪所大学时对我说的话。他当时对我们的讨论很厌烦，说：“没有所谓正确的决定，只要你做了决定就是正确的。”这话太对了。因为你永远不知道生活会发生什么。你只需专注于当下正在做的事，不留遗憾。十年后你不会说：“要是当初接受了那份工作就好了。” 你的人生成功取决于你如何对待自己做出的决定。

turns.speaker: Lenny
turns.en: So if you feel regret about something, this is a good one to pull out of just I will make this the best I can make it, and that's all the best I can do.
turns.zh: 所以如果你对某件事感到后悔，这句话很管用——尽最大努力把它做到最好，这就是你能做的最好的了。

turns.speaker: Tamar Yehoshua
turns.en: You can move forward.
turns.zh: 然后继续前进。

turns.speaker: Lenny
turns.en: Move forward. I love that. Last question, I know you're a parent. I'm a new parent. I have a 14-month old at this point. Is there a piece of parenting advice that you learned early on that you think might be helpful to me or folks that are new parents or something you've just learned yourself that you think might be helpful?
turns.zh: 向前看。我喜欢这种态度。最后一个问题，我知道你也是为人父母。我刚当上新手爸妈，目前孩子14个月大了。有没有早期学到、觉得对新手父母有帮助的育儿建议，或者自己最近领悟到的好方法？

turns.speaker: Tamar Yehoshua
turns.en: 14 months. I think the best parenting book I read besides the How to Talk So Your Kids Will Listen & How to Listen so Your Kid Will Talk is, I think it's called Healthy Sleep Habits, Happy Baby. We are much happier when we sleep well. We perform better at work when we sleep well. Children need to sleep. So making sure that they sleep well. And sometimes that's like, I did the whole sleep training, cry until you fall asleep and my kids still speak to me. So it was okay. That is the basic things. Make sure that their basic needs are met and then as they grow up, share your life with them. So a piece of advice I was given was analogous to Talk so your Kids Will Listen is when they had come home from school. You can't just say, "How was your day?" Say, "You know what? I did a podcast with this person and it was super interesting because they talked about this or that." Or, "I'm massively screwed up and I should have asked them this or that." And they'll be like, "Oh my God, I was at school today and this is what happened." If you share your life with them, they will share their life with you.
turns.zh: 14个月。我认为除了《如何让孩子听话》和《如何让孩子开口说话》之外，我读过的最好的育儿书籍是《健康睡眠习惯，快乐宝宝》。睡眠充足能让我们更快乐，睡眠充足也能提升工作效率。孩子需要睡眠，所以要确保他们能睡好。有时我会采用整夜哭闹训练法，但孩子还是会跟我说话。不过没关系。关键在于满足他们的基本需求，随着他们长大，要与他们分享生活经历。有人给我的建议类似于《如何让孩子听话》中的做法——比如他们放学回家时，你不能只问“今天过得怎么样？”而是说：“你知道吗？我今天和某某人做了播客，内容特别有趣，他们谈到了某某事。”或者说：“我这次真是彻底搞砸了，本该问他们某某事的。”这样他们就会说：“天哪，我今天在学校遇到了这种情况。”如果你和他们分享生活，他们也会和你分享。

turns.speaker: Lenny
turns.en: Such good advice. I really appreciate it. Tamar, thank you so much for being here. You're awesome. We got through so much great stuff. Everything I was hoping we get through. Two final questions. Where can folks find you if they want to read up on more stuff that you share and just follow you online and how can listeners be useful to you?
turns.zh: 这些建议太棒了。真的很感激。塔玛，非常感谢你能来参加节目。你太棒了。我们探讨了好多精彩内容，完全符合我的期待。最后两个问题：如果听众想了解更多你的分享、在网上关注你，应该去哪里找你？

turns.speaker: Tamar Yehoshua
turns.en: Find me on LinkedIn and I have a subject called Practical Intelligence where I've been interviewing practitioners who are working with AI. It was my way of learning. I started when I was a VC. Trying to continue doing it. And how can I be helpful if you are a customer of Glean, I'd love to know what you think, what works and what does more.
turns.zh: 在领英上找我，我的账号叫“实用智能”，我一直在采访使用AI的从业者。那是我学习的方式，之前我还是风投时就开始了。现在还在继续做。如果你是Glean的客户，我很想听听你们的反馈，哪些方法有效，哪些有待改进。

turns.en: What's the best way to share that with you? Is it like messaging on LinkedIn, subscribe to Substack?
turns.zh: 怎么跟你分享？是通过领英消息，还是订阅Substack？

turns.speaker: Tamar Yehoshua
turns.en: Message on LinkedIn, or comment on your-
turns.zh: 领英消息，或者在你的——
